# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.

**discovered-from:AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG** (epic AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV).

## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.
data.title: Vite dep-cache hygiene: 95 orphaned deps_temp_* dirs (158 MB) in node_modules/.vite

# Align AI_Hell's test framework with the Tableau-Card-Engine game repos

AI_Hell runs a bespoke Vitest setup: `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.projects.ts` with a
static classifier (`classifyTestFiles` / `isIntegrationTest` in `vitest.projects.ts`)
splitting test files into `unit` / `integration` projects, and test roots `src/`,
`scripts/`, `vite/` — there is **no top-level `tests/` directory**. Every sibling TCE
game repo (and the scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) uses the
standard layout: a `unit` project in `vite.config.ts` with
`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']` and no per-file classifier.

**Goal:** bring AI_Hell's test layout and project selection into line with the sibling
repos so cross-repo conventions, agent/audit tooling expectations (top-level `tests/`
tree), and the test skill's type profiles apply uniformly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No test lost or doubled.** After migration, AI_Hell's full suite runs the
   identical set of `*.test.ts` files currently selected by
   `vitest.projects.ts::allTestFiles` (src/, scripts/, vite/) — same count and same
   per-file project membership; verified by a before/after selection diff.
2. **Standard layout adopted.** Tests live under a top-level `tests/` tree laid out to
   match sibling repos (e.g. `tests/deploy/` for infra guards, `tests/<area>/`),
   selected via the standard include globs in `vitest.config.ts` (or the config file's
   `test.projects`), with `tsconfig.json` including `tests/**/*.ts`.
3. **Isolation preserved.** Phaser/DOM-booting tests retain their separation from the
   fast node `unit` project (the deliberate unit/integration split — parent
   AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV, blocked child AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ). Alignment must NOT flatten
   Phaser-heavy tests into the node unit project or regress suite runtime. The
   `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard is updated to assert the new layout and
   still passes.
4. **Tooling keeps working.** The test skill's per-type profiles
   (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, `.pi/test-config.json`) remain
   functional — update only if project names/commands change, and verify each type
   (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) runs.
5. **Documentation updated.** Comments in the vitest config(s), AGENTS.md and any
   dev notes reflect the new layout. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill).
6. **Full suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- Refactor only — no change to app behaviour.
- Preserve the deterministic membership guard pattern (`vitest.projects.ts` is
  deliberately the single source of truth for selection; keep an equivalent guard).
- This item may also relocate `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (added by the watch-ignore
  port, MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0) into `tests/deploy/` for full parity — sequence after or
  alongside that port.

## Related work

- MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0 — Port Vite watcher-ignore to sibling game repos (discovering item; adds `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` under the current layout)
- AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV — parent of the unit/integration split decision
- AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ — Unit/integration Vitest project split (blocked)
- AH-0MV53ABBU008FKE0 — Test-skill runner no-ops: no .pi/test-config.json suiteCommands for vitest (completed)

# Intake brief — Explosions should be explosions (image-based explosion VFX)

> **Source request (verbatim):** "The explosions right now are just multiple
> circles. They look OK but we can improve them a great deal. Make them actual
> explosion images that change shape as they shrink. Each should be a subtle
> variation on the red/orange explosion colour."

## Problem statement

Every destruction burst is still rendered as a cloud of small filled circles,
so explosions read as "a lot of dots" rather than as an explosion. Replace the
circle particles with image-based explosion shapes whose silhouette changes as
they shrink and fade, tinted from a red/orange fire palette with subtle
per-particle variation.

## Users

- **Player** — the primary user; perceives destruction feedback.
  - *As a player, when I destroy an enemy or lose my ship, I see a recognisable
    explosion (a hot core, ragged flame lobes, sparks) rather than a spray of
    dots, so combat impact feels real and satisfying.*
- **Developer / designer** — tunes the look without touching gameplay code.
  - *As a developer, I can adjust the fire palette, frame count, morph timing
    and particle counts through named exported constants in one shared module
    and verify the behaviour deterministically in unit tests.*
- **Agent / maintainer** — must be able to change the look once.
  - *As a maintainer, I know the game and every gym consume the same VFX code,
    so a look change cannot drift between the game and the gym scenes.*

## Decisions pending producer confirmation

These three questions materially change the implementation and are recorded as
**OPEN QUESTION** entries in the Appendix. The ACs below assume the
**recommended** option for each, so the brief is implementable as written if the
producer accepts all recommendations.

1. **Art source** — procedural runtime-generated explosion textures
   (**recommended**) vs. committed raster sprite sheets vs. Graphics-only
   morphing polygons.
2. **Colour policy** — all explosions move to a red/orange fire palette
   (**recommended**) vs. keep the current per-entity hue and add a hot
   red/orange core vs. red/orange for enemy deaths only.
3. **Coverage** — every `spawnExplosionParticles` call site (**recommended**:
   enemy/boss/player deaths, victory fireworks, wave-timeout penalty, gyms) vs.
   entity-death bursts only.

## Existing state

- All destruction VFX route through one shared module,
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` (`spawnExplosionParticles()`), used by
  `BaseEnemy`, `Boss`, `CombatCoreScene._spawnPlayerExplosion`,
  `playerDeathJuice`, `endOfRunJuice` (victory fireworks/defeat) and the gyms
  (via the shared combat core), so game↔gym parity already holds.
- A burst is a **single Phaser `Graphics`** animated by one tween; each frame
  redraws every live particle as `fillCircle(p.x, p.y, p.radius)` with a
  colour from `jitterColor(baseColor)` (HSL jitter ±`EXPLOSION_HUE_JITTER_DEG`
  = 20° around the exploding entity's palette colour). Particles fade
  (`1 - fadeStep·elapsed`) and shrink over `EXPLOSION_LIFESPAN_MS` (400 ms).
- Three patterns exist (`radial`, `ring`, `implosion`) mapped per entity in
  `EXPLOSION_PATTERNS_BY_TYPE`; counts scale with entity size (clamped 8–80).
- Determinism: all jitter is drawn from a seeded PRNG (`createRng(seed)`), and
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts` pins geometry, colour bands, counts,
  jitter and the Phaser integration through a structural scene double.
- Live per-kind counts are exposed by `getExplosionVfxCounts()` /
  `resetExplosionVfxCounts()` and consumed by the action-intensity metric.
- The repo ships **no image assets** today: `public/` contains only audio
  (`public/audio/sfx/*.wav`); every other visual is drawn procedurally
  (Graphics / shapes). Audio assets are baked from ToneForge recipes by
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`.
- Documentation of the current circle rendering lives in
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.1–§7.2 (particle-effects and
  explosion-patterns bullets) and `README.md` ("Explosion VFX (particle
  bursts)").

## Desired change

1. Replace circle particles with **explosion imagery**: a small set of
   explosion shapes (e.g. 4–6 frames per burst family) whose silhouette changes
   over the burst's life as the particle shrinks and fades, so the explosion
   visibly *evolves* (hot dense core → ragged flame lobes → thin embers)
   instead of uniformly shrinking dots.
2. Use a **red/orange fire palette** with subtle variation per particle
   (hue/lightness jitter inside a constrained warm band, plus a brighter
   white-hot core), rather than the current entity-hue tinting.
3. Keep the existing pattern system (`radial`, `ring`, `implosion`), counts,
   lifespan, seeded determinism, teardown/registry contract and per-kind
   counters intact — this is a rendering/feel change, not a gameplay change.
4. Apply the change through the single shared module so the game and every gym
   get it automatically (no divergent copies).

## Acceptance Criteria

> AC1–AC3 depend on the recommended decisions (procedural textures, red/orange
> palette, all call sites). If the producer chooses another option, the ACs are
> revised before implementation.

- [ ] **AC1 — Explosion imagery replaces circles.** `spawnExplosionParticles()`
  renders each particle as an explosion shape from a cached, shared texture/frame
  set (no per-frame `fillCircle` particle rendering); a burst visibly reads as a
  blast (core + lobes/embers), not as a cloud of circles.
- [ ] **AC2 — Shape changes as the particle shrinks.** Each particle's shape
  frame is a deterministic function of its normalised age, so the silhouette
  morphs through at least 3 distinct frames from spawn to expiry while the
  particle also scales/shrinks; the final state is a thin ember, not a dot.
- [ ] **AC3 — Red/orange fire palette with subtle variation.** All explosion
  colours derive from exported warm-palette constants; 100% of emitted particle
  colours fall inside the documented red/orange hue band with bounded
  saturation/lightness variance (asserted across every colour the module emits,
  including cores, for both death bursts and victory fireworks).
- [ ] **AC4 — Behaviour preserved.** Pattern assignment, size-scaled counts
  (8–80), `EXPLOSION_LIFESPAN_MS`, seeded reproducibility (same seed ⇒ identical
  frames/colours/positions), the `opts.registry` teardown contract, the
  `getExplosionVfxCounts()` increments/decrements, the `delay`/`depth`/`scale`
  options and the null-scene guard all behave exactly as before.
- [ ] **AC5 — Single shared implementation / parity.** The change lives only in
  the shared VFX module (+ its texture helper); the game and every gym use it
  with no duplicated rendering code, and the repo-wide duplicate-body guard
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and gym-parity docs
  assertions still pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — Deterministic, headless-testable tests.** Unit tests cover frame
  selection/morph progression, colour-band invariants, determinism, teardown and
  counters without a real WebGL canvas (texture provider is injectable/stubbable
  and preserves the existing structural scene double), and an in-game/gym visual
  verification is documented (GymFodderEnemies death bursts, player death,
  victory fireworks).
- [ ] **AC7 — Performance budget.** Concurrency stays bounded: no per-particle
  texture generation, frame textures are generated once and reused, and no
  regression in particle counts or teardown (no leaked display objects after
  scene SHUTDOWN/restart).
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation updated.** GDD §7.1–§7.2 (particle effects,
  explosion-patterns/colour table), the README "Explosion VFX (particle bursts)"
  section and the module header/comments describe the image-based look, palette
  and frame/morph constants, replacing the "small filled circles",
  "Hues stay recognisably 'that ship'", and per-entity colour statements.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No new runtime dependency**; stay on Phaser primitives.
- **Zero-asset repo convention** (recommended option): generate the explosion
  textures at runtime from code, cached by key; do not commit binary art unless
  the producer chooses the sprite-sheet option.
- **GDD §7.1 style rule**: "Geometric, angular shapes … No organic forms".
  Literal photographic/smoke-puff explosion images would conflict; the
  recommended look is a stylised neon blast (angular/ragged polygon lobes) to
  stay within the established art language — the producer may override.
- **Gym↔game parity** (repo convention / AGENTS.md): one shared code path.
- **Determinism**: seeded PRNG only; no `Math.random()` in VFX.
- **Performance**: bursts can be dense (Boss layers 3 patterns, victory
  fireworks up to 30 staggered bursts); textured particles must not multiply
  draw calls per particle in a way that breaks the current action-intensity
  budget. Use shared textures + batched images, and keep the existing count
  clamps.
- **Scope discipline**: gameplay numbers (damage, counts, timing, SFX) are out
  of scope; extra ideas are recorded as linked work items, not folded in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — replace the Graphics circle renderer with a
  pre-generated/cached explosion frame texture provider and per-particle
  image/quad rendering whose frame is a function of normalised age; add the
  warm-palette constants + colour resolution; keep the pure geometry/PRNG,
  pattern, lifecycle, registry and counter contracts.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts` — extend/extend-and-rename the pure-state
  and Phaser-double tests for frames, morph progression, colour band,
  determinism, teardown and counters.
- `src/vfx/explosionTextures.ts` (new, predicted) — procedural frame generation
  (deterministic polygon/blob silhouettes per frame) plus the texture cache/
  keyed registry and a headless-safe seam.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — the warm fire palette constants (or keep them in the
  VFX module, following the module's existing constant-export convention).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.1–§7.2 particle-effects and explosion
  pattern/colour text.
- `README.md` — "Explosion VFX (particle bursts)" section.
- Call sites that need no code change but must be visually verified:
  `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`, `src/entities/Boss.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`,
  `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` (victory fireworks).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Ambiguity risk** — the colour request may mean "keep ship identity but make
  the blast feel fiery". If the producer picks the recommended full red/orange
  palette, per-entity identity (Scout green, Diver yellow, Phaser magenta,
  player cyan) is intentionally lost and the GDD tables must change; this is
  recorded as an explicit assumption rather than silently decided.
- **GDD style conflict risk** — "no organic forms" vs. explosion images; the
  recommended stylised-neon-blast silhouette keeps the language, but a producer
  preference for realistic puffs would require an art pipeline.
- **Performance risk** — replacing one Graphics with N images per burst could
  regress frame time in dense scenes (Boss + fireworks). Mitigation: shared
  cached textures, a bounded texture count, batched rendering, and a check of
  the action-intensity/perf capture before review.
- **Test harness risk** — texture generation needs a canvas; the recommended
  procedural option must expose an injectable provider so headless Vitest runs
  stay deterministic and do not need WebGL.
- **Scope-creep risk** — tempting extras (screen-shake per particle, heat
  distortion, sound layering, per-entity explosion image families) are recorded
  as linked follow-up items, not added here.
- **Assumption** — the operator's "each should be a subtle variation on the
  red/orange explosion colour" refers to per-particle colour variation inside a
  warm palette, not a single flat orange.

## Related work

- **Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player deaths**
  (AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V) — the parent feature that introduced the circle-based
  particle bursts this item replaces visually.
- **Explosion pattern emitters and combinator** (AH-0MTVID632005ACBF) —

## Goal

Crash resilience for dev telemetry: with the dev JSONL sink moving to an in-memory per-run buffer (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3), a page reload or crash mid-run loses the un-uploaded tail. Streaming telemetry batches to the dev server during the run — instead of one run-end upload — bounds that loss to at most one flushed batch (~64 records, ~1.3 s of play) and removes the page-reload regression that localStorage previously masked.

## Context

- Parent/related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3 (in-memory dev sink; this item is explicitly deferred there).
- Current flow: the JsonlTelemetrySink buffers records in memory, flushes batches of 64 to the sink, and the whole run is POSTed once at run end (`uploadDevTelemetry`). A crash before that POST loses the entire run's telemetry; a reload also loses the buffer entirely once it is no longer localStorage-backed.
- Dev only: the same reasoning applies to the production remote sink, which already streams batches via `HttpTelemetryTransport` (with retry/backoff), so production is not affected.

## Proposed design

- Send each flushed batch to the dev endpoint as it is produced (`POST /api/telemetry/upload`) instead of (or in addition to) the run-end upload.
- The server (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`) currently stores each upload as one complete `session-<stamp>.jsonl` and runs the automatic evaluation per upload; a per-batch POST would create many tiny recordings and repeated evaluations. The endpoint (or a new `part` protocol) must therefore either:
  - append JSONL records to the run's open session file keyed by a run id/seed, and evaluate once at run end, or
  - keep the run-end upload and add a lightweight "heartbeat/checkpoint" mechanism that only recovers the tail on demand.
- UX/offline: batches sent while the dev server is unreachable should stay in the memory buffer (or a bounded queue) and be retried at run end; at most one batch may be lost on a hard crash.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A mid-run crash/reload followed by a run-end state loses no more than one flushed batch (~64 records / ~1.3 s) of telemetry; the rest is recoverable from the dev server.
- AC2: The server session file for a run contains its records exactly once (no duplication from partial + final uploads), and the automatic evaluation still runs once per run.
- AC3: Dev CLI tooling (`record-session`, `capture-gameplay`, `verify-dev-telemetry`) continues to work unchanged in behaviour.
- AC4: Full project test suite passes.

## Status

Open decision item — parked until the in-memory sink (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3) lands. Do not implement concurrently with that item in the same worktree.

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

# Intake brief — Compiled videos cannot be fast forwarded (AH-0MVMIK8EM001JAYR)

## Headline

Videos produced by `npm run capture` (MediaRecorder WebM/VP9+Opus) are
written **without a Duration element, SeekHead or Cues (seek index)**, so VLC
cannot fast-forward, seek, or even display a usable timeline for them. The fix
is a packet-preserving (`-c copy`) seek-index remux of every successful
capture output before it is delivered.

## Problem statement

Chromium's `MediaRecorder` writes a WebM stream whose Segment Info omits
Duration and whose clusters carry no external Cues/SeekHead index. Most
players tolerate this, but VLC does not: fast-forward/seeking fails,
`ffprobe` reports `duration=N/A`, and the timeline is unusable. Verified on
real capture outputs under `capture-output/` — e.g.
`capture-output/gameplay-2026-10-09T21-32-12-740Z-1.webm` has zero Cues and
zero SeekHead elements (`duration=N/A`), while the ffmpeg-compiled promos
(`capture-output/promo.webm`, `highlight-01.webm`) carry all three and are
seekable (`duration=57.896` etc.).

## Users

- The developer/producer reviewing captured gameplay footage (full runs,
  batch iterations, scenario clips, multi-scene stitched WebMs) in VLC or
  other external players.
- Any consumer of the shipped/archived WebMs who needs to scrub or fast-forward
  them without re-encoding.

User story: *As a developer reviewing captured gameplay, I want to fast-forward
and scrub through the WebM in VLC, so I can jump straight to the segments I
need instead of watching the whole clip.*

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Seekable output**: A WebM produced by `npm run capture` (with an ffmpeg
   available on the host) reports a finite non-zero total duration via
   `ffprobe -show_entries format=duration` (`format.duration`), and its EBML
   structure contains a Cues seek index plus SeekHead referencing Info,
   Tracks and Cues — verified per clip by the capture tool's existing probe.
2. **No quality/content change**: The remux is packet-preserving
   (`-c copy` — no re-encode of VP9 or Opus); codecs, stream layout, and
   decoded frame/timeline content are unchanged (verify codec + duration
   equivalence against a pre-fix capture).
3. **All capture paths benefit**: single clip, `--count` batch iterations,
   `--all-scenarios` scenario clips and the `capture:scenes` multi-scene
   stitched WebM all go through the same sink-finalise seam and are all
   seekable (they share `recording.finalise({ success: true })`).
4. **Graceful degradation**: When no ffmpeg binary can be resolved (this is
   the documented zero-ffmpeg capture environment), the capture still
   succeeds and writes the current unseekable WebM, with a clear warning
   naming the fix and how to enable it — never a hard failure that breaks
   the no-ffmpeg story.
5. **Tests + docs**: Hermetic unit tests for any new pure logic (remux
   invocation argc/verification without real footage), plus an
   integration/e2e verification on a small real clip asserting duration +
   Cues + SeekHead presence; `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (known-limits and
   output sections) and code comments updated; full project test suite passes
   with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Existing documented design decision (docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md
  "No MP4 output (ffmpeg)" and `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` header): "the
  capture path never invokes a system ffmpeg". The recommended approach (a)
  keeps that constraint intact by using only the Playwright-bundled binary;
  Open Question 1 records the producer decision.
- Playwright (an existing devDependency, installed by the documented
  `npm run capture:install`) ships a **bundled ffmpeg binary** that performs
  the `-c copy` seek-index remux correctly (verified: the bundled
  `ffmpeg-linux` from the ms-playwright cache produced Duration + Cues +
  SeekHead and `duration=1.895` on a real capture). This is the recommended
  remux tool — no system install needed.
- Long-run clips can be ~1.8 GB; the sink architecture was built to keep node
  memory O(one chunk). A remux pass must stream through ffmpeg (or equivalent)
  and must not buffer the whole clip in node memory.
- Salvaged `.partial.webm` outputs are documented failure paths, not
  deliverables — out of scope.
- UK English in all written output.
- Backfill of already-captured WebMs is out of scope unless the producer
  requests it (recorded as a separate linked item if wanted).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep**: a pure-JS EBML rewriter or a backfill/`--seekable` CLI is
  larger than the reported bug. Keep the fix to the minimal remux at the
  finalise seam; record extras as linked work items, not scope.
- **Remux failure on huge clips**: a failed remux must not destroy the raw
  capture — write the remuxed file to a temp path and only swap it in on
  success (mirroring the existing `.partial.webm` rename discipline).
- **ffmpeg resolution portability**: resolution order (env → PATH → bundled
  Playwright ffmpeg) must be deterministic and documented; the bundled
  binary path depends on Playwright's install revision, so resolve it
  through the Playwright API rather than hard-coded paths.
- **Validation parity**: structural checks (duration + Cues + SeekHead) are
  automated via ffprobe; a manual VLC fast-forward check on the operator's
  machine is the final behavioural confirmation.
- **Assumption**: the reported VLC behaviour is caused by the missing
  Duration/Cues/SeekHead (confirmed structurally; see Problem statement).
  Compiled promo outputs are unaffected as they are already ffmpeg-produced.

## Existing state

`npm run capture` drives a headless Chromium page: `canvas.captureStream(60)`
→ `MediaRecorder` (VP9/Opus, 8 Mbps), chunks streamed via a bounded sink
(`scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs`) to `<stem>.partial.webm`, renamed into
place by `finalise({ success: true })`. Chromium writes no Duration/Cues.
The promo compiler (`compile-promo.mjs --compile`) already re-encodes/remuxes
its deliverables through a full ffmpeg, so promo/highlight/showreel outputs
are already seekable — only raw capture outputs are affected.

## Desired change

Attach a seek-index remux step at the sink-finalise seam so every successful
capture WebM is made seekable before it is delivered. **Decided approach (a):**
resolve the **Playwright-bundled** ffmpeg first (it is installed by the
documented `npm run capture:install` and is verified to perform this remux),
falling back to `FFMPEG_BIN`/`FFPROBE_BIN` env overrides and then PATH
(mirroring `compile-promo`'s `resolveTools()`), run
`ffmpeg -i <in>.webm -c copy <out>.webm`, swap the result in only on success,
and warn (without failing the capture) when no ffmpeg can be resolved. This
keeps the documented "never invokes a **system** ffmpeg" constraint intact.
Verification reuses the existing probe seam (`capture-probe.mjs`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` — `finalise()` seam where a seek-index
  remux would attach (or a sibling module invoked from it)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — the two sink finalise call sites
  (single-clip ~L1991 and multi-scene ~L2554); recorder setup ~L2753
- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — `resolveTools()` ffmpeg-location pattern and
  the `-c copy`-style argv precedent to reuse
- `scripts/capture-probe.mjs` — existing probe seam to extend for
  duration/Cues verification
- `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.test.ts` (+ new tests) — hermetic coverage
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — update known-limits/output sections

## Related work

- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** — Spike: automated gameplay video capture
  (headless browser + scripted bot); established the capture pipeline.
- **AH-0MUZQG13S006KL8K** — Capture: video join + highlight selection;
  established output artefacts and the raw-WebM format.
- **AH-0MVDV4OKN001OT18** — Pure edit-plan/selection logic in compile-promo;
  supplies the ffmpeg-driving pattern (incl. `resolveTools`).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documents the "no system ffmpeg in the
  capture path" constraint and the output/probe contract.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (ANSWERED — producer decision): **How should the seek-index remux relate
  to the documented "the capture path never invokes a system ffmpeg"
  constraint?** Options:
  - (a) Remux by default using the Playwright-bundled ffmpeg. The bundled
    binary (installed by the documented `npm run capture:install`) already
    performs the `-c copy` seek-index remux correctly (verified on a real
    capture: Duration + Cues + SeekHead, `duration=1.895`), so no *system*
    ffmpeg is required and the documented constraint stands literally.
    Degrade gracefully when it cannot be resolved.
  - (b) Remux by default, requiring a full system ffmpeg (compile-promo's
    `resolveTools()` path) and hard-failing the delivery when absent.
  - (c) Pure-JS EBML rewrite (patch Info/Duration, prepend SeekHead,
    append Cues) with no binary dependency at all.

  **Recommended: (a)** — smallest change, verified working, packet-preserving,
  no new dependency, and it preserves the documented constraint. `(b)` breaks
  the zero-ffmpeg capture story; `(c)` is a materially larger new
  WebM-rewriting surface (with 1.8 GB streaming-copy risk) for no benefit the
  bundled binary does not already give.

  **Answer (producer): (a)** — remux by default using the Playwright-bundled
  ffmpeg with graceful degradation. Source: interactive reply to the question
  comment (`intake - question ...` on AH-0MVMIK8EM001JAYR). The brief,
  ACs and Key Files stand as written; no further changes needed.

- Resolved without asking (answerable from repo convention — recorded as
  intake decisions, not open questions):
  - **Default vs opt-in**: the remux runs by default on every successful
    capture, because the report is about the default `npm run capture`
    output. No `--seekable` flag and no backfill command in scope.
  - **Tool resolution**: env override → bundled Playwright ffmpeg → PATH,
    following compile-promo's existing `resolveTools()` pattern
    (`FFMPEG_BIN` / `FFPROBE_BIN` first).
  - **Out of scope**: salvaged `.partial.webm` failure artefacts; backfilling
    already-captured files.

Pending the producer's answer to Q1 the brief stands as written (all
acceptance criteria are behavioural and hold under any of the three
options); the item is flagged for producer review.

**Q1 answered: (a)** — Playwright-bundled ffmpeg remux by default with
graceful degradation. The brief, ACs and Key Files are final and stand as
written.

## Problem

Candidate D's *States* section (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Candidate D → States) defines a ring win as **all six hexes held and the AI's massed counter-attack on the hangar repelled**, and a campaign loss as **the hangar falls** (the last hex taken and the hangar's own defence failing). The MVP build (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE) deliberately ships the narrower rule, decided by the producer on 2026-10-30 (intake question Q2 = a):

- **Ring secured = every hex of the current ring held.** The next ring then opens.
- **No massed hangar assault** is resolved or played.
- **No hangar-falls lose state**: the hangar itself can never be lost in the MVP, so a player cannot lose the campaign.

As a player, I want the ring to end with a real fight for the hangar — a massed AI counter-attack I have to repel, and a defeat condition that means the hangar can actually fall — so that holding the whole ring feels like a victory rather than the start of the next checklist.

# Intake Brief — SFX on mini-boss explosions

**Work item:** AH-0MVVEI7FD004TR2M (feature, medium)
**Headline:** Give the mini-boss defeat explosion sweep its missing audio: the
mini-boss body plays a boss-scale death cue on the defeat frame, every planned
sweep burst fires a cue scheduled to land with its own visual burst (thinned and
voice-limited so ~60 bursts cannot clip the mix), and the 20-burst finale
(2 every 0.25 s) reads as the loudest moment of the sequence.

**Source request (verbatim):** "We have plenty of explosions when the miniboss is
killed, but there are no SFX accompnaying them"

**Producer decisions (settled 2026-10-31, all three answered "A"):**
**Q1 = (a) reuse existing baked cues only** — no new ToneForge recipe or asset;
**Q2 = (a) one cue per burst with per-role thinning** — every escort burst,
every 2nd scatter/anchored burst, both voices of every finale pair;
**Q3 = (a) visual-timed** — each cue scheduled at its burst's own `delayMs`,
never quantised to the 16th-note accent grid.

## Problem statement

Defeating a mini-boss already produces a large visual display — the shared death
sweep (`src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts`) fires one burst per swept escort
plus `max(0, 30 − n)` scattered bursts, 10 anchored bursts around the death point
and a 20-burst finale (two every 250 ms) — but **not one of those bursts makes a
sound**. The mini-boss's own body also dies silently: the mini-boss is not routed
through the shared enemy-kill seam (`finaliseEnemyKill`), so it never reaches
`playDestructionSound()`, and it has no `playDestructionAudio` of its own. The
result is a ~5 s victory moment that plays out in near-silence against a busy
combat mix, so the biggest kill in a level reads as weaker than a routine enemy
kill.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, when I finally kill the mini-boss I want the whole
  screen of explosions to *sound* like the biggest thing I have done in the
  level, so the victory lands instead of trickling past."
- **Player (headphones / low volume)** — "As a player, I want the cascade to be
  dense but never a clipped wall of noise, so I can still hear the score, my own
  weapons and the next wave's telegraphs."
- **Developer/tester (gym)** — "As a tester, when I press EXPLODE in the
  mini-boss gym I want to hear exactly the audio that ships in the game, so audio
  parity is verifiable in one click."
- **Producer / audio designer** — "As the producer, I want the cue choices and the
  density policy to be named, tunable constants in one shared place, so I can
  retune the moment without touching gameplay code."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Every planned burst is voiced, in sync with its visual (Q1=a, Q3=a).**
  The shared sweep is the single audio dispatch point: each planned burst that
  passes the thinning rule dispatches exactly one cue scheduled at that burst's own
  `delayMs` (so audio lands with the burst it belongs to, never on the global
  16th-note grid), and the mini-boss's own body plays `playBossDestructionSound()`
  exactly once on the defeat frame. Neither an unplanned burst nor a burst the
  thinning rule drops ever produces a cue, so the thinning rule is the only reason a
  planned burst is silent.
- **AC2 — Density is bounded and tunable in one place (Q2=a).** The thinning rule
  is per role, exported as `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_SFX_*` constants with no inline tuning
  literals: **every** `enemy` burst, **every 2nd** `scatter` and `anchored` burst,
  and **both** voices of every `finale` pair (2 per 250 ms). Per-role volume scales
  are exported constants too, with the finale the loudest layer. The existing per-cue
  voice limiter (4 voices / 150 ms) stays the hard backstop; a test asserts the
  dispatch count per 250 ms window stays within the documented bound for the
  maximum 60-burst plan, and that the finale is never thinned.
- **AC3 — Reuse-only, documented cue palette (Q1=a).** No new ToneForge recipe,
  no new baked asset, no manifest change: body → `playBossDestructionSound()`;
  `enemy` / `scatter` / `anchored` bursts → `playDestructionSound()` cue family
  (its 3 baked variants); `finale` bursts → `playVictoryExplosionSound()` (its 4
  baked variants, drawn deterministically from the run seed). The choices are
  recorded in the GDD §7.3 row and are audibly distinct from
  `playPlayerDestructionSound()`; the cue-manifest contract suite still passes
  unchanged.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity, no divergent copy.** Both `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss`
  get the audio from the one shared executor; neither scene contains its own cue
  logic. The repo duplicate-body guard
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs
  assertion pass.
- **AC5 — Safe no-op and deterministic.** Headless tests, muted SFX, volume 0 and
  autoplay-blocked browsers play nothing and never throw. Cue/seed selection draws
  from the run-seeded RNG carried in the plan (no `Math.random()` in the planner),
  so the same seed replays the same audio; an injectable `playSound` seam lets
  tests record dispatch without audio hardware.
- **AC6 — Validation.** New unit tests cover: one cue per kept burst at the
  burst's delay, the thinning/limit bounds at the 60-burst maximum, the body cue
  firing exactly once, the final-vs-escort volume relation, the no-op/mute paths,
  and seed determinism; the docs tests for the updated GDD §7.3 row pass.
- **AC7 — Documentation.** GDD §7.3 SFX Event Catalog gains a mini-boss-defeat
  row (character, volume, lead time), `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` and
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` are updated as applicable, and the module JSDoc records the
  density policy and the reason for any divergence from the 16th-note accent grid.
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes**, via the
  dev-push gate (never an ad-hoc full run).
- **AC9 — The victory hold is not delayed (constraint).** Audio never gates the
  sweep's completion: `onComplete` still fires from the last burst's own tween as
  today, with SFX enabled, with SFX muted/blocked by autoplay policy and when the
  injected `playSound` seam throws, so the reward-overlay hold of
  AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z (AC3/AC6) is unchanged. A test asserts `onComplete` fires
  exactly once in each of those cases and that no cue is dispatched after the
  sweep handle is `stop()`ped.

## Constraints

- Audio is build-time baked ToneForge WAVs played through the single shared
  `AudioContext`; no procedural synthesis (the thruster hum is the only
  exception). **Reuse-only (Q1=a): no new recipe, no new bake, no manifest change.**
- The planner must stay Phaser-free, pure, total and deterministic — the cue
  choice belongs in the plan; only the executor talks to the scene.
- The sweep is cosmetic: no gameplay, score, drop, telemetry or wave-accounting
  change, and the reward overlay hold (parent AC3/AC6 of AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z)
  must be unaffected — audio must not delay `onComplete`.
- The mini-boss must never acquire audio by being routed through the
  reward-bearing enemy-kill seam (that would resurrect score/drop/telemetry for
  swept entities, forbidden by AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z AC4).
- Gym↔game parity is mandatory (AGENTS.md); any intentional divergence must be
  recorded on this item and in a code comment.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — shared planner + executor, consumed by
  `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:3272`) and
  `GymMiniBoss.explodeRandom` (`src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts:315`). Bursts carry
  `role: 'enemy' | 'scatter' | 'anchored' | 'finale'`, `delayMs`, position,
  colour, `particleCount`, `scale`, `lifespanMs`. **No audio anywhere**; the only
  injectable seam is `options.onComplete`.
- `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` — no audio of any kind; `takeDamage()`/`destroySelf()`
  are silent, and swept escorts are removed via `destroySilently()` (no cue).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — the cue layer. Relevant existing cues:
  `playDestructionSound()` (enemy fall, beat-quantised via `playExplosionCue`),
  `playBossDestructionSound()` (0.6 s saw 180→20 Hz, the full boss death),
  `playVictoryExplosionSound()` / `playVictoryCrackSound()` /
  `playVictoryPopSound()` (multi-seed, `options.delay` + `options.volume`),
  `playPlayerDestructionSound()`. Volume-scale constant precedent:
  `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`, `PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`,
  `HOLD_FULL_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`.
- `src/audio/cueVoiceLimiter.ts` — per-cue cap of 4 voices per 150 ms applied once
  at the `playCue` funnel.
- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` — precedent for sounding a multi-burst display:
  a per-burst sound player seam (`playVictoryFireworkCue`), a per-play volume and
  an `ENDOFRUN_VICTORY_FIREWORKS_SOUND_EVERY_N` thinning knob (currently `1`).
- Docs: GDD §7.3 (SFX Event Catalog + beat-synced accents),
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md`
  (heavy-one-shot RMS tier 0.090, peaks ≤ 0.50), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

## Desired change

1. Extend the pure planner so each planned burst carries its audio decision
   (cue + baked-variant seed + volume scale + whether the thinning rule keeps it),
   derived from its `role`, the run seed and the thinning rule — so the plan stays
   deterministic and fully testable without Phaser. Settled palette (Q1=a):
   `enemy`/`scatter`/`anchored` → `playDestructionSound` family;
   `finale` → `playVictoryExplosionSound` family.
2. Extend the executor with an injectable sound seam
   (`options.playSound?: (burst, cue) => void`) defaulting to a real dispatcher in
   `src/audio/effects.ts` (e.g. `playMiniBossSweepSound(role, options)`), scheduling
   each kept cue at the burst's own `delayMs` (Q3=a, visual-timed) — the same way
   `spawnVictoryFireworks` schedules its cues.
3. Play `playBossDestructionSound()` for the mini-boss body on the defeat frame,
   from the same shared seam, exactly once.
4. Export the tunables (`MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_SFX_ENABLED`, per-role volume scales,
   per-role thinning (
   `enemy` 1, `scatter` 2, `anchored` 2, `finale` 1), voice budget) as constants in
   the sweep module and document them in the module JSDoc.
5. Tests + docs as listed in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — plan gains a per-burst audio descriptor (`cue`, variant seed, volume, kept-by-thinning); executor gains the `playSound` seam and schedules each kept cue at the burst `delayMs`; new exported SFX tunables.
- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.test.ts` — one cue per kept burst at the right delay, thinning/limit bounds at 60 bursts, finale never thinned, body cue once, determinism, no-op seam.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — role→cue dispatcher (`playMiniBossSweepSound`) + volume constants, built on the existing `playCue` options; no new synthesis, no manifest change.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` / `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts` — dispatcher coverage: cue mapping, volume scaling, mute/volume-0 no-op, never throws.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 — new mini-boss-defeat SFX row (character, volume, lead time) and a note on why the cascade is visual-timed rather than 16th-note-quantised.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — record that the sweep reuses existing cues (no new recipe/asset).
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — `GymMiniBoss` row note that the sweep's audio is shared (only if the row's wording needs it).

> `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` / `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` are **not**
> modified either: the cue-manifest contract suite is the guard that proves the
> palette is reuse-only (Q1=a) — it must keep passing unchanged.
>
> `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` and `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md` are **not** touched:
> the body cue is dispatched from the shared defeat seam and no asset is baked
> (Q1=a).

## Related work

- **AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z — Mini Boss explosions** (completed, high): the parent
  request that created the visual sweep (scope split, 30 extras, 10 anchored,
  20-burst finale, reward held until completion). This item adds the audio layer to
  exactly that display and must not change its timings or the reward hold.
- **AH-0MVROEKMT005RVML — PlayScene mini-boss defeat sweep wiring**,
  **AH-0MVROEJJR002HDLS — Verification tests for mini-boss death sweep**,
  **AH-0MVROELN600410GP — PlayScene mini-boss defeat sweep wiring**,
  **AH-0MVROEMUO007Z3RY (GymMiniBoss sweep)**,
  **AH-0MVROEO2I0014ILM — Mini-boss defeat sweep documentation** (all completed):
  the module, its tests, its scene wiring and its docs that this change extends.
- **AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 — Explosions timed with the beat** (completed): the
  16th-note accent quantisation + per-tick cap used by enemy destruction cues; this
  item departs from it for the sweep (display-timed) and must say so.
- **AH-0MVH8RQR7007QG8E — Limit the number of each explosion and weapon sound that
  can fire** (completed): the per-cue voice limiter that is the cascade's hard
  backstop.
- **AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 — Massive Explosions and Fireworks on Victory** (completed):
  the precedent for per-burst SFX on a planned multi-burst display
  (`playVictoryFireworkCue`, per-play volume, `..._SOUND_EVERY_N` thinning).
- **AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q — Balance the levels of all enemy sounds** /
  **AH-0MVCRR10A001OM2K** (completed): the heavy-one-shot RMS tier (0.090) and peak
  ceilings a new cue must respect.
- **AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J — Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to
  ToneForge** (completed): the baked-asset-only constraint.
- **AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY — Explosions should be explosions** (open, medium): the
  visual counterpart; if it changes burst visuals, the audio timing here is
  unaffected (audio is driven by `delayMs`, not by burst shape).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — cacophony.** 60 bursts over ~5 s voiced naively is a clipped wall;
  mitigated by per-role thinning, per-role volume scales and the existing 4-voice /
  150 ms per-cue limiter, all pinned by a test at the 60-burst maximum.
- **Risk — audio/visual desync.** Using the beat-quantised
  `playExplosionCue` seam would shift cues up to 187.5 ms off their bursts and drop
  most of them at the 4-per-tick cap; the settled decision (Q3=a) is to schedule by
  `delayMs` (visual-timed), recorded as a deliberate departure in the GDD row.
- **Risk — the mini-boss body cue steals the finale's impact.** If the body cue is
  the loudest element on frame 0, the 20-burst finale stops reading as a climax;
  mitigated by the settled per-role volume scales making the finale the loudest
  per-burst layer (Q2/Q3 = a).
- **Risk — the sweeps regain reward semantics.** Voicing the mini-boss through
  `finaliseEnemyKill` would award score/drops/telemetry; the shared defeat seam is
  used instead (AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z AC4).
- **Risk — pausing.** Cues scheduled with `delay` must not outlive a scene
  shutdown mid-sweep; dispatch at spawn time (Phaser handles the schedule) and rely
  on the existing scene-teardown mute path, asserted by a test.
- **Assumption —** no new asset is needed (Q1 = a, settled): the existing cue
  families already cover the moment.
- **Assumption —** the audio is dispatched from the shared sweep seam, not from
  `PlayScene`/`GymMiniBoss`, because parity is mandatory.
- **Scope-creep guard.** A per-burst voice-limiter retune, any new recipe
  (explicitly declined in Q1), background music for the mini-boss
  (AH-0MVKXT7O70061FXU) and any visual change to the sweep are **out of scope**;
  they are recorded as linked work items rather than absorbed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (ANSWERED): Which cue palette? — Answer (producer, interactive reply
  2026-10-31): **(a) reuse existing baked cues only** — body
  `playBossDestructionSound`, sweep bursts `playDestructionSound`, finale
  `playVictoryExplosionSound`; no new ToneForge recipe or asset. Options offered:
  (a) reuse only; (b) reuse + a new dedicated `playMiniBossDestructionSound`
  recipe; (c) reuse but one heavy `playBossDestructionSound()` climax. Agent's
  advisory recommendation was (a). Source: producer reply on this item.
- Q2 (ANSWERED): How dense should the cascade be? — Answer (producer, interactive
  reply 2026-10-31): **(a) one cue per burst with per-role thinning** — every
  escort burst, every 2nd scatter/anchored burst, both voices of every finale pair.
  Options offered: (a) per-burst with thinning; (b) per-burst with no thinning;
  (c) body + finale pairs only. Agent's advisory recommendation was (a). Source:
  producer reply on this item.
- Q3 (ANSWERED): Visual-timed or beat-quantised? — Answer (producer, interactive
  reply 2026-10-31): **(a) visual-timed** — each cue scheduled at its burst's own
  `delayMs`; the sweep does not route through the 16th-note accent grid. Options
  offered: (a) visual-timed; (b) beat-quantised. Agent's advisory recommendation
  was (a). Source: producer reply on this item.
- Q4 (answered from repo context, no producer input needed): Should the gym get the
  audio too? — **Yes**; AGENTS.md gym↔game parity is mandatory and
  `GymMiniBoss.explodeRandom` already runs the shared executor, so the audio comes
  from the shared module. Source: `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (GymMiniBoss row),
  `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts:315`.
- Q5 (answered from repo context): Is there already a mini-boss death cue to reuse?
  — **No**: `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` has no audio and the GDD §7.3 catalog has no
  mini-boss-defeat row. Source: repo search for `sound|audio|cue` in
  `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3.
- Q6 (answered from repo context): Must the audio be baked assets rather than
